prompt:
I need the front end for Wellshare. Simple record-keeping software for small volunteer-run rural water associations to log meter readings and bill members.

Who's using it: Gordon Pruitt, 71, a retired surveyor and the volunteer treasurer of a 58-household mutual water association that shares two wells. He's meticulous with numbers but not very fast with software.

What they're doing right now: It's mid-November, and two volunteers walked the meter routes over the weekend and handed him their paper sheets. Gordon is entering all 58 readings for the October 15–November 15 cycle. He needs the software to catch typos and impossible values, such as a reading lower than last month's or a jump that looks like a leak. He'll correct or annotate each flagged one, then lock the cycle so bills can go out by the 20th.

What's in the system at this point: 58 service connections on 2 routes (North Ridge, 31 meters; Creek Road, 27). Each has a member name, meter ID (e.g., WM-0217), previous reading in gallons, a 12-month average, and status (active, vacant, seasonal). Cycle Oct 15–Nov 15, 2026. Rates: $38 base covers the first 3,000 gal, then $4.10 per 1,000 gal. Known issues: meter WM-0233 (Halvorsen) was replaced Oct 28, so its count restarts from 0. The Delgado household reported a burst pipe on Nov 3. Two seasonal cabins are expected to read near zero. Last cycle, 3 typos were caught after bills went out. Volunteer readers: Sue Marsh (North Ridge), Ben Cho (Creek Road).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
